headline: A mild, dry start gives way to increasing Wednesday clouds; rain and gustier wind reach Central Kentucky Wednesday night while the Upstate stays mainly dry
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Surface high pressure, a dry lower atmosphere and northwest flow aloft support sunshine and mild afternoons through Tuesday. The high shifts east Wednesday as a northern-stream shortwave digs toward the Ohio Valley and begins phasing with southern-stream energy. Low pressure then organizes over the western Ohio Valley, increasing southwest flow, clouds and moisture. Central Kentucky should remain dry through most of Veterans Day before rain arrives Wednesday evening and becomes likely overnight into early Thursday.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 9:15 AM EST, KDVK reported 50°F with a 41°F dew point, calm wind, visibility above 10 miles and clear sky. At 8:54 AM, KLEX reported 46°F with a 39°F dew point, west wind near 7 mph, visibility above 10 miles and clear sky. The earlier Frost Advisory was no longer active at the final NWS point-alert check.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Danville at issuance; the earlier Frost Advisory was no longer active at the final check. Independent concerns are localized late-night frost and patchy river-valley fog in favored Bluegrass drainage areas; a widespread freeze or dense-fog event is not expected.
days.forecast: Morning frost ends quickly, followed by sunshine with a few high clouds. Dry air and light west wind allow a most-likely Danville high near 63°F. Wind stays mainly 2–7 mph with gusts below 15 mph. Tonight is clear and chilly as the boundary layer decouples. The most-likely Danville low is near 37°F, with the maintained KDVK cold correction and terrain supporting lower to middle 30s in favored hollows. Localized frost is possible late. HRRR and RAP profiles support patchy river-valley fog mainly from about 2–8 AM Tuesday, but widespread or dense fog is not expected.

days.label: Tuesday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert currently covers Tuesday or Tuesday night. No threshold independent hazard is expected. A few sheltered rural locations may see patchy frost or shallow valley fog late Tuesday night, but widespread freezing conditions are unlikely.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny weather continues as the upper flow becomes briefly more zonal. A weak southern-stream wave passes well to the south, but the column over the Bluegrass remains too dry for rain. Southwest wind runs 5–10 mph with gusts around 12–20 mph, supporting a most-likely Danville high near 67°F. Tuesday night stays mostly clear with a most-likely low near 39°F after the established KDVK low correction. Fog and frost should remain patchy and confined to the coldest drainage locations.

days.label: Veterans Day / early Thursday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert currently covers Wednesday night. Independent concerns are a period of rain and strengthening southwest-to-west wind after sunset. A few rumbles of thunder are possible, but SPC forecasts no organized severe threat and heavy or flooding rain is not expected. The sharper cold change follows later Thursday, mostly beyond this forecast window.
days.forecast: Veterans Day begins dry with filtered sunshine, then clouds thicken as the polar and subtropical jets interact and low pressure develops toward the western Ohio Valley. Southwest wind increases to 5–12 mph during the day, with a most-likely Danville high near 65°F. The leading rain band should reach the Bluegrass after roughly 7 PM, although model timing still varies by a few hours. Rain becomes likely overnight, with primary rainfall around 0.05–0.25 inch through early Thursday. Wind turns west toward dawn, sustained 8–15 mph with gusts mainly 18–30 mph. Temperatures settle into the lower to middle 40s rather than reaching their colder post-frontal values before the 72-hour endpoint.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays sunny and mild today and Tuesday, with most-likely Danville highs near 63°F and 67°F and nighttime lows near 37°F and 39°F. Veterans Day starts dry and reaches about 65°F before clouds thicken. Rain becomes likely Wednesday evening and overnight, accompanied by gustier wind. No official point alert was active at issuance; the much colder air and any later-week flakes remain beyond this 72-hour forecast.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather through Tuesday and today’s temperature; moderate-high on Tuesday temperatures; moderate on patchy valley fog, Wednesday’s high and nighttime rain onset; moderate-low on isolated thunder and the exact overnight wind maximum

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: High pressure and a dry lower atmosphere keep the Clemson–Central corridor sunny and warmer than normal through Wednesday. Clear nights and light wind still favor strong radiational cooling and large station-to-station differences, especially between Clemson and the colder drainage terrain near Central and Pickens. The approaching Ohio Valley system increases high cloud and southwest flow Wednesday night, but limited moisture and a weakening southern fringe keep the primary rain chance low until early Thursday.
upstate.currentConditions: At 9:15 AM EST, KLQK reported 51°F with a 48°F dew point, calm wind, visibility above 10 miles and clear sky. At 8:54 AM, KCEU reported 53°F with a 44°F dew point, calm wind, visibility above 10 miles and clear sky. Earlier mist near KCEU and KAND dissipated by about 8 AM. No official NWS point alert was active for Clemson or Central at the final check. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert is active for Clemson or Central. Independent concern is limited to localized grass frost in the coldest Central/Pickens hollows and isolated lake or river-valley fog late tonight. A widespread freeze or dense-fog event is not expected.
days.forecast: Morning mist has cleared, leaving full sunshine under dry high pressure. The most-likely high is near 72°F at both Clemson and Central. Wind is northwest or variable at 0–6 mph with gusts below 12 mph. Tonight becomes clear and calm. Applying the maintained station corrections gives most-likely lows near 44°F at KCEU and 39°F at KLQK. This morning’s brief mist and an isolated RRFS saturation signal support about a 20% chance of localized fog from roughly 3–8 AM Tuesday, but broader guidance remains too dry for widespread restrictions.

days.label: Tuesday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert is active. No threshold independent hazard is expected. A small late-night valley-fog chance remains, but freezing temperatures, thunder and meaningful rain are not expected.
days.forecast: Mostly sunny sky continues, with occasional high cloud possible. Light wind becomes southwest at 0–6 mph with gusts below 12 mph. The most-likely high is 71°F at Clemson and near 70°F around Central. Tuesday night is partly cloudy and chilly. Bias-corrected station centers are about 46°F at KCEU and 41°F at KLQK, with roughly a 10–15% chance of localized valley fog toward dawn Wednesday.

days.label: Veterans Day / early Thursday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert is active. No threshold independent hazard is expected. A light shower is possible late Wednesday night or early Thursday, but thunder, heavy rain and advisory-level wind are not expected before the 72-hour endpoint.
days.forecast: Veterans Day remains mostly sunny through the afternoon with a most-likely high near 71°F at Clemson and 70°F around Central. High cloud increases after sunset as the upstream trough and cold front approach. Southwest wind is 0–5 mph during the day, becoming west-southwest at 3–8 mph overnight and increasing toward 5–15 mph with gusts of 12–22 mph near dawn Thursday. A light shower is possible after about 1 AM, with the best chance from 4–8 AM. Primary rainfall is only a trace to 0.03 inch. Most-likely lows are near 51°F at KCEU and 46°F at KLQK. The stronger front and colder air arrive later Thursday, mostly outside this forecast.

upstate.bottomLine: The Upstate remains sunny and dry through Wednesday daytime. Most-likely highs are about 72°F today, 70–71°F Tuesday and 70–71°F Wednesday. Bias-corrected nighttime centers are KCEU 44°F, 46°F and 51°F and KLQK 39°F, 41°F and 46°F. Only localized fog or sheltered frost is possible tonight, followed by a 20% light-shower chance late Wednesday night into early Thursday.
upstate.confidence: High on the dry and warm daytime pattern; high on Monday’s high; moderate-high on Tuesday and Wednesday temperatures; moderate-high on station lows; moderate-low on localized fog and the early-Thursday shower chance

sourceNotes: OFFICIAL ALERTS: no active NWS point alert was present for Danville, Clemson or Central at the final issuance check. The earlier Central Kentucky Frost Advisory was no longer active. Official alerts remain explicitly separate from SPC/WPC outlooks and this independent analysis.

The 11:12Z Louisville discussion keeps Central Kentucky dry through Tuesday under high pressure and northwest-to-zonal flow, then develops an Ohio Valley low as polar and subtropical jet energy interacts. It expects rain late Wednesday into Thursday, limited moisture return, less than 0.50 inch through Friday and only a later outside flurry chance after the forecast window.

The 11:23Z Greenville-Spartanburg discussion keeps dry high pressure and rising heights over the Upstate through midweek, with highs 5–10°F above normal, large diurnal ranges and frost focused mainly in North Carolina. It also acknowledges brief lake-area low stratus and mist this morning.

Chris Bailey’s exact November 9 Kentucky Weather Center post, ‘A Small Taste of Winter Possible Late This Week,’ was consulted as accepted authoritative source material. Bailey calls for 60–65°F today, similar Tuesday weather, increasing and thickening clouds with gustier southwest wind Wednesday, showers entering western Kentucky during the afternoon/evening and rain/wind sweeping east Wednesday night. Details absent from the post or unreadable in its graphics were left unknown.

Latest official observations showed clear sky and unrestricted visibility at KDVK and KLEX after a frosty morning. KCEU, KLQK, KAND and KGSP were also clear after earlier Clemson/Anderson-area mist dissipated. Tempest was excluded.

College of DuPage 13:41–13:46Z radar and satellite imagery showed both forecast regions dry and largely cloud-free. The 13Z surface analysis showed high pressure and no nearby boundary; 12Z 500-mb, 850-mb dewpoint and precipitable-water analyses showed dry northwest/confluent flow and a moisture-poor lower atmosphere.

Central Kentucky official guidance and the full model cluster support most-likely Danville highs near 63°F, 67°F and 65°F. The maintained KDVK −2°F low correction, official point guidance and drainage terrain support most-likely lows near 37°F and 39°F the first two nights; Wednesday-night temperatures hold in the lower/middle 40s while rain and wind arrive.

Wednesday timing is the main Central Kentucky uncertainty. Bailey and readable GFS/Canadian graphics keep central/eastern Kentucky dry during Wednesday afternoon, while the NWS point forecast raises rain sharply after 7 PM. GFS/NBM/RRFS and local BUFKIT bring light QPF Wednesday night; ECMWF is several hours slower. The candidate therefore uses 10% or less daytime, 80–90% overnight and a three-hour timing tolerance rather than treating the spread as an unresolved material conflict.

Upstate Monday guidance splits between a 68–69°F ECMWF/RRFS branch and a 72–75°F NWS/NBM/GFS/GEFS/HRRR/RAP branch. Clear satellite imagery, strong insolation and the maintained operational weighting favor a 72°F center while the calibrated 70–74°F range retains the cooler edge.

Upstate coarse global and GEFS overnight grids remain too warm for KLQK drainage conditions. Most-likely lows use NWS/NBM plus the maintained KCEU +2°F and KLQK −3°F corrections. Ten-degree card widths describe the Clemson-to-Central and terrain spread, not uncertainty at one exact sensor.

For early Thursday in the Upstate, GFS is the 0.18-inch wet outlier, ECMWF/NBM are dry, RRFS produces about 0.02–0.04 inch and GEFS has a 0.012-inch median with strong timing dispersion. This supports a 20% late-night shower chance and trace–0.03 inch primary QPF, with no thunder.

SPC Days 1–3 forecast no organized severe-thunderstorm area for either region. WPC Day 1’s excessive-rainfall risk is confined to far southeastern Texas, and Days 2–3 are below 5% nationwide. These national outlooks are not point alerts.
The locally extracted Central Kentucky GRIB package was generated at 2026-11-09T14:24:00Z. Every model is used only within its validated horizon; partial HRRR/RAP periods are not extrapolated.
Local GRIB disclosure: hrrr: hrrr ends at 2026-11-11T12:00Z and is partial-horizon guidance for this 72.0-hour window.
Local GRIB disclosure: rap: rap ends at 2026-11-11T12:00Z and is partial-horizon guidance for this 72.0-hour window.

The active BUFKIT 19 installation was refreshed with GFS 06Z, HRRR 11Z, RAP 12Z and operational RRFS 06Z profiles. KLEX/KSME bracket Danville; KAND/KGSP are regional Upstate proxies rather than exact KCEU/KLQK profiles.

NAM and NAM 3-km operational production ended after the 12Z November 3 cycle under NWS Service Change Notice 26-47. Retained cycles are stale and were excluded; RRFS is explicitly identified as the operational replacement and given a limited supplemental share until local verification samples accumulate.
The latest cumulative accuracy summary contains 127 verified of 135 checkpoints and all-category accuracy of 80% overall, including 83.6% for Central Kentucky and 76.3% for the Upstate.

The 48-hour checkpoint for forecast 20261107T1337Z became due at 13:37Z, but GitHub’s scheduled 14:15Z verification run had not started at issuance and therefore was not yet incorporated. This candidate uses the latest completed accuracy summary and must be rechecked against main before publication; if the summary changes in a way that affects validation or adjustments, the candidate must be regenerated under a new forecastId.

Current station corrections, empirical lead-specific temperature widths, regime-aware model weights, explicit fog/rain timing and official-alert separation were applied. KDVK high remains monitoring with no adjustment; low corrections applied are KDVK −2°F, KCEU +2°F and KLQK −3°F.

Temperature cards use the current calibrated regional widths: Kentucky high/low widths of 5/9°F, 5/8°F and 7/8°F; Upstate widths of 4/10°F, 5/10°F and 6/10°F. Prose gives narrower most-likely station values.
All local times use Eastern Standard Time. The third card explicitly covers Wednesday night and early Thursday because validThrough is exactly 72 elapsed hours after issuance.
